skill.name: pubchem-database
skill.description: Query PubChem compounds, properties, structures, annotations, and bioactivity through PubChemPy or PUG-REST. Supports identifier, similarity, substructure, and batch workflows.
skill.summary: Search and analyze PubChem compound and bioactivity records.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Static detections for Markdown backticks, PubChem identifiers, and official documentation links are false positives; they do not execute commands or inspect the host system. Network calls are expected PubChem access and do not transmit credentials, but the fixed binary write can overwrite structure.png in the current directory. No prompt injection, covert exfiltration, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: The structure image example overwrites structure.png without checking whether the file already exists.
remediation.suggestion: Check for an existing file and require explicit overwrite approval, or generate a unique destination name.

content.value_statement: Chemical identifiers and assay records are difficult to retrieve and compare consistently. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through focused PubChem queries and structured interpretation.
actual_capabilities: Search PubChem compounds by name, CID, SMILES, InChI, or molecular formula.
Retrieve molecular properties, synonyms, structure identifiers, and annotation sections.
Run similarity and substructure searches with result limits and thresholds.
Query compound bioassays, assay targets, active compounds, safety data, and drug information.
Download compound structures in SDF, JSON, or PNG formats and compare batches.
limitations: Requires internet access and sends queries to PubChem or PubChemPy endpoints.
Depends on PubChem availability, rate limits, record quality, and third-party package behavior.
Similarity and substructure searches can take time and may return large result sets.
Results are research data and do not replace expert chemical, clinical, or safety review.

use_cases.title: Profile a Known Compound
use_cases.description: Resolve a compound name or CID, then collect identifiers, physicochemical properties, synonyms, and selected annotations.

use_cases.title: Compare Compound Collections
use_cases.description: Retrieve consistent properties for a list of compounds and highlight missing values or likely screening constraints.

use_cases.title: Investigate Bioactivity Evidence
use_cases.description: Find assays, targets, and active compound records for a target or reference compound.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Compound
prompt_templates.prompt: Find {compound} in PubChem. Return its CID, formula, molecular weight, IUPAC name, canonical SMILES, and InChIKey.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner lookup for one known compound

prompt_templates.title: Compare Properties
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare {compound list} using molecular weight, XLogP, TPSA, hydrogen-bond counts, and rotatable bonds. Clearly mark unavailable values.
prompt_templates.scenario: Property comparison across a small set

prompt_templates.title: Search Related Structures
prompt_templates.prompt: Use {compound or SMILES} for a PubChem similarity search at {threshold}. Limit results to {count} and summarize key property differences.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Bioactivity Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate {target or CID}. Connect relevant assays, active compounds, targets, safety annotations, and evidence gaps while respecting PubChem rate limits.

output_examples.input: Find aspirin by name and summarize its identifiers.
output: Returned formula, molecular weight, IUPAC name, SMILES, InChI, and selected synonyms.
Marked any unavailable fields and identified PubChem as the source.

output_examples.input: Compare caffeine, aspirin, and ibuprofen for common molecular properties.
output: Presented a compact comparison of molecular weight, XLogP, TPSA, hydrogen-bond counts, and formula.
Highlighted missing values and avoided treating simple property rules as clinical conclusions.

output_examples.input: Find compounds related to a reference SMILES and review bioactivity.
output: Applied the requested similarity threshold and result limit.
Summarized candidate CIDs, structural identifiers, selected properties, linked assays, and evidence gaps.

best_practices: Use CIDs for repeated queries and record the identifier used for each result.
Set thresholds and maximum record counts before similarity, substructure, or assay searches.
Check missing fields, source annotations, and retrieval dates before drawing research conclusions.
anti_patterns: Do not treat PubChem records or simple property filters as medical or safety advice.
Do not launch unbounded searches or rapid request loops that exceed PubChem limits.
Do not overwrite downloaded files without confirming the destination and existing content.

faq.question: Does this skill require an API key?
faq.answer: No API key is required for standard public PUG-REST requests. PubChem usage limits still apply.

faq.question: Which compound identifiers are supported?
faq.answer: The documented workflows support names, CIDs, SMILES, InChI, and molecular formulas. Available operations vary by identifier type.

faq.question: Can it search by chemical structure?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents similarity, substructure, and superstructure workflows, with thresholds and result limits where supported.

faq.question: Can it retrieve bioactivity and safety information?
faq.answer: Yes. It can query assay summaries, targets, active compounds, PUG-View safety sections, and drug annotations when PubChem provides them.

faq.question: Does it write files?
faq.answer: Yes. Download examples can create SDF, JSON, or PNG files. Confirm the destination before allowing overwrites.

faq.question: Are the results suitable for clinical decisions?
faq.answer: No. PubChem data supports research and screening. Qualified experts must verify identity, evidence quality, hazards, and clinical relevance.
